knowledge-base.name: lang-swift
knowledge-base.triggers: Swift, .swift, Package.swift, Package.resolved, SwiftUI, UIKit, AppKit, Combine, SwiftLint, swift-format, XCTest, SPM, Swift Package Manager, iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, Vapor, Hummingbird
knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific idioms, guardrails, and patterns for Swift 5.9+. Loaded automatically when agents work on .swift files or Package.swift. Applies to iOS, macOS, server-side Swift, and CLIs. Covers value semantics, protocol-oriented design, safe optional handling, structured concurrency with async/await, and testing with XCTest.

core-principles.principle: Prefer structs over classes. Use classes only when identity or inheritance is required.
Compose behavior through protocols and extensions rather than class hierarchies.
Unwrap with `guard let` or `if let`. Force-unwrap (`!`) is forbidden outside tests and IBOutlet declarations.
Use async/await and task groups. Avoid raw GCD queues for new code.
Enable strict concurrency checking. Treat warnings as errors in CI.

guardrail.rule: Never force-unwrap (`!`) outside of tests and `IBOutlet`/`IBAction` declarations. Use `guard let`, `if let`, or nil coalescing instead.
guardrail.bad: let user = userCache[id]! // crashes at runtime if nil let url = URL(string: rawString)!
guardrail.good: guard let user = userCache[id] else { return fetchUser(id: id) } guard let url = URL(string: rawString) else { throw NetworkError.invalidURL(rawString) }

guardrail.rule: Never use `DispatchQueue.main` or raw GCD in new code. Use `@MainActor` for UI-bound code and `async/await` for all asynchronous operations.
Use `actor` for mutable shared state. Never use `var` properties on classes that are accessed from multiple threads without a lock or actor isolation.
Enable strict concurrency checking. Types crossing actor isolation boundaries must conform to `Sendable`. Never use `@unchecked Sendable` without a lock or proof of thread safety.
Always handle `Task.isCancelled` or call `Task.checkCancellation()` in long-running async work. Unresponsive-to-cancellation tasks cause memory leaks and hangs.
Mark classes `final` by default. Remove `final` only when subclassing is explicitly designed for and documented.
guardrail.bad: class UserService { } // implicitly open to subclassing

guardrail.rule: Use `TaskGroup` / `ThrowingTaskGroup` for parallel fan-out instead of multiple unstructured `Task` instances. Structured concurrency ensures all child tasks are awaited.
Use completion handler-free APIs. Never write new APIs using completion handlers when the caller can use async/await. Convert legacy callbacks with `withCheckedThrowingContinuation`.
guardrail.bad: func fetchUser(id: String, completion: @escaping (Result<User, Error>) -> Void) { }
guardrail.good: func fetchUser(id: String) async throws -> User { }

guardrail.rule: Define protocols where they are consumed, not where they are implemented. Keep protocols focused — prefer multiple small protocols over one large one.
Prefer `some Protocol` (opaque types) over `any Protocol` (existentials) when the concrete type is fixed at the call site. Existentials incur heap allocation and lose static dispatch.
Pin package versions with `.upToNextMinor(from:)` for libraries. Commit `Package.resolved` for applications; omit for libraries.
Use `guard let` for early exit when the unwrapped value is used afterward. Use `if let` for scoped unwrapping within a branch only.
Use `Self` instead of repeating the type name inside type definitions. Improves resilience to renaming and inheritance.
Run `swift format` or SwiftLint before every commit. Enforce `force_cast`, `force_unwrapping`, and `force_try` as errors in SwiftLint configuration.

project-structure.description: Swift Package Manager layout for library and CLI targets.
project-structure.layout: MyProject/ ├── Package.swift # Manifest (targets, dependencies, platforms) ├── Package.resolved # Locked versions (commit for apps, omit for libs) ├── Sources/ │ ├── MyProject/ # Main library target │ │ ├── Models/ │ │ ├── Services/ │ │ ├── Protocols/ │ │ └── Extensions/ # TypeName+Capability.swift │ └── MyProjectCLI/ # Executable target (thin entry point) │ └── main.swift ├── Tests/ │ └── MyProjectTests/ └── README.md

rules.rule: `main.swift` or `@main` struct should be thin: parse arguments, build dependencies, call library code
All business logic in library targets — testable without running the binary
One primary type per file; file named after the type

pattern.name: Optionals: guard let and if let
pattern.context: Any optional unwrapping — prefer guard let for early exit

pattern.name: Result type for typed errors
pattern.context: Expected failures — network, parsing, domain rules
pattern.description: Typed errors in Result allow callers to handle failure paths without try/catch. Prefer when errors are expected and recoverable.

pattern.name: Protocol extensions with default implementations
pattern.context: Shared computed behavior across conforming types

pattern.name: Actor for shared mutable state
pattern.context: Any cache, registry, or counter accessed from multiple tasks

pattern.name: Async/await with task groups
Property wrappers
pattern.context: Reusable property constraints — clamping, validation, persistence

pattern.name: Sendable conformance
pattern.context: Types passed across actor isolation boundaries

pattern.name: Package.swift essentials
pattern.context: New Swift packages — minimum viable manifest

testing.framework: XCTest (built-in); Swift Testing (Swift 5.10+) as modern alternative

rules.rule: Use protocol-based mocks injected via initializer — no singletons in tests
Async tests use `async throws` directly (no XCTestExpectation for async/await code)
Test both success and failure paths for every public method
All bug fixes include a regression test

swiftlint-config.description: Enforce these rules as errors in .swiftlint.yml.
swiftlint-config.example: # .swiftlint.yml force_cast: error force_unwrapping: error force_try: error function_body_length: warning: 40 error: 50 cyclomatic_complexity: warning: 8 error: 10

quick-reference.item: Prefer structs; classes only for identity or inheritance
Banned — use guard let / if let / nil coalescing
async/await + actors; no DispatchQueue in new code
Use actor for all mutable shared state — not locks or queues
Types crossing isolation boundaries must conform to Sendable
Always check Task.isCancelled in long-running loops
withThrowingTaskGroup for parallel operations, not unstructured Tasks
Classes are final by default; remove only when subclassing is designed
Define at consumption site; keep small; use composition
some Protocol over any Protocol when type is fixed
Commit for apps, omit for libraries
swift format + SwiftLint in CI; force_* rules as errors
